transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM), Jordan Ellis (CTO, NovaHealth), Ava Martinez (SRE Lead), Samir Patel (PM), Elena Gomez (Compliance)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through the weekly POC sync. quick agenda — results recap, then rollout planning for canary/A-B, cutover steps, monitoring and runbook owners.
[00:14] Jordan: Yep, sounds good. We've got Ava and Samir on for the SRE and PM perspectives and Elena for compliance.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Quick note, I'll kick off with the results, Liam will cover the latency/cost breakdown and then we'll move to canary.
[00:30] Liam: Alright, so high level — last week's test window shows 95th percentile latency at ~210ms for the hosted model variant, p50 around 72ms, token cost delta relative to baseline about +13%. We did see improved throughput with prefix caching enabled; KV cash — I mean KV cache — reduced repeat prefix tokens by roughly 22%.
[00:52] Ava: Wait did you say 210ms p95 on hosted? For our peak we need below 250ms so that's okay but what about tail spikes during burst events?
[01:05] Liam: We did a burst test up to 600 rps and saw tail spikes up to 420ms in one window when autoscaler was spinning new workers. We have an autoscale tune suggestion in the sheet. Link: https://redwood.company/s/poctest/results-sheet
[01:22] Samir: How confident are we that the caching patterns will be similar in production? Our traffic has a lot more session-based repeats but also some long-context flows for clinical notes.
[01:33] Maya: Good question. We recommended enabling both prefix cache and KV cache for sessions and keeping a small dedicated mempool for long contexts. Liam, are the quant settings we ran applicable?
[01:40] Liam: Yes, the int8 quant profile we used is stable for the 2B model; for longer contexts the KV eviction policy needs to be tuned — otherwise you'll see regen latency. We also recommended the canary use the quantized variant then fallback to full float if timeouts hit.
[01:57] Elena: From compliance — we need to confirm KMS integration and that audit logs show model inputs for 30 days. Is that covered by Redwood Private?
[02:07] Priya: We covered KMS in the doc and Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs with retention options. I'll share the SOC2 evidence pack and KMS integration guide after the call.
[02:20] Jordan: Cool. Let's move to rollout approach. We want minimal user impact. Samir, what segments are we thinking for canary?
[02:28] Samir: Proposal: start with 3% of traffic for 72 hours, then 10% for another 72, run A-B on feature toggles for 10k requests, monitor quality and latency. If metrics look good, ramp to 50% then full cutover in a controlled window.
[02:42] Maya: That aligns with our recommendations. We usually suggest 5% for the first window but 3% is fine. Key is automated rollback triggers. Liam, what should the triggers be?
[02:53] Liam: Suggested triggers: p95 latency > 500ms sustained for 10 minutes; error rate increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes; quality regression on synthetic eval set — BLEU/ROUGE drop > 3 points or specific prompt failure rate > 1%. We'll feed these into the canary pipeline.
[03:12] Jordan: For the quality checks, can we run daily evals against our regression suite and fail the canary if there's a regression?
[03:19] Liam: Yes, we can wire the eval harness to the deployment pipeline. It takes ~18 minutes for the full suite today but we can run a smaller smoke eval every 30 minutes for canary.
[03:28] Ava: On monitoring — we need dashboards and alerts in our Grafana and paging integration with Opsgenie. Liam, do you have dashboard queries you can share?
[03:36] Liam: I will share a Grafana JSON and recommended alert thresholds. I'll include token-level cost panels and per-route latency. Suggested alerts: p95 > 400ms (warning), p95 > 500ms (critical), 5xx rate > 0.5% (critical).
[03:52] Maya: Also add a runbook doc that lists step-by-step rollback: 1) divert traffic back to baseline model, 2) scale up baseline pool if needed, 3) open support incident with Redwood and attach logs. Who owns the runbook?
[04:05] Ava: NovaHealth SRE will own the runbook execution; Redwood to provide the runbook and run a dry-run with us.
[04:12] Priya: We'll schedule a dry-run — suggest do it during a low traffic window. We'll provide step-by-step runbook and playbook for rollbacks and fallbacks.
[04:20] Samir: For cutover timing, we'd like to do final ramp in a maintenance window next month, target 2025-08-03. Is that OK?
[04:27] Maya: Tentatively yes, subject to the canary results and compliance sign-off. Elena, any blockers for Aug 3?
[04:34] Elena: Need to validate encryption at rest and KMS tests. Also want a run-through of audit log retention. If Redwood can provide the evidence pack and the test plan we'll be fine.
[04:45] Liam: Quick note about infra — if you run in Dedicated vs Private, networking differs. For Private with VPC peering there's an extra setup step for the KMS endpoint. We have docs but it adds ~2 days of infra work.
[04:58] Jordan: We prefer Private for PHI handling. We'll budget the infra time.
[05:04] Maya: On cost: enabling prefix cache reduces tokens but increases memory usage; the pricing delta for canary at 10% is estimated at +7% for the test window because of double writes during canary. We'll send a detailed delta.
[05:16] Samir: Need to see the actual numbers — include token counts and estimated monthly cost at steady state.
[05:22] Maya: We'll attach the spreadsheet. Also note fallback policies — automatic fallback to baseline floater variant if error criteria met.
[05:30] Jordan: One more question on observability — can we get per-tenant traces that show model input/output redaction?
[05:37] Priya: Yes, we support token-level redaction and per-tenant tracing; we'll show how the trace links map to logs in the SOC2 pack.
[05:45] Ava: For the dry-run, suggest we test failure scenarios: KV eviction, slow worker spin-up, auth failures to KMS. We want to validate rollback in each case.
[05:56] Liam: We'll simulate those in a staging run. For KV eviction the metric to watch is cache hit ratio and regen latency. We'll add guided checks in the runbook.
[06:05] Jordan: Ok, next steps recap?
[06:08] Maya: Redwood to send: final canary runbook + timeline (Maya), updated pricing delta (Maya), Grafana dashboards + alert JSON (Liam), SOC2/KMS docs (Priya). NovaHealth to schedule dry-run and confirm on-call (Ava) and finalize segments (Samir).
[06:24] Elena: I'll review the compliance docs once they come in and flag anything else.
[06:29] Maya: Anything else?
[06:32] Samir: Minor thing — we had a note about model fallbacks causing slight tone shifts in responses; product wants to monitor for UX drift during A/B.
[06:40] Liam: We'll add a small human-eval sample in the canary smoke suite to detect drift.
[06:45] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and set the dry-run date.
[06:50] Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes / Artifacts referenced: https://redwood.company/s/poctest/results-sheet, POC runbook draft (shared), SOC2 evidence pack (to be shared).
